statement.ja: 母音に後続する -hci/-hcin では直前の長母音は短母音化し、派生的な末子音 -h に後続する場合は -ahci/-ahcin の前で基底の p, t, k が現れる。

entailment.quote: With the vowel-following forms, if the preceding vowel is long, it becomes short, and with the consonant-following forms, if the final consonant is a derived -h, the underlying p, t, or k surfaces.

anchor.exact: If the -hci attaches to an auxiliary verb that follows the main verb, it does not attach to the main verb.

statement.en: When -hci attaches to an auxiliary verb following a main verb in Karafuto Ainu, it does not attach to the main verb.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語において、本動詞に後続する補助動詞に -hci が付く場合、本動詞には付かない。

conditions: when attaching to an auxiliary verb

entailment.quote: If the -hci attaches to an auxiliary verb that follows the main verb, it does not attach to the main verb.

anchor.exact: In an adnominal modification structure, -hci is often used, but there are a few examples of its not being used.

statement.en: In an adnominal modification structure in Karafuto Ainu, -hci is often used, but occasionally omitted.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語の連体修飾構造において、-hci はしばしば用いられるが、用いられない例も少数ある。

entailment.quote: In an adnominal modification structure, -hci is often used, but there are a few examples of its not being used.

anchor.exact: When co-occurring with a conjunction, the -hci is omitted from the first verb.

statement.en: When co-occurring with a conjunction in Karafuto Ainu, -hci is omitted from the first verb.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語において、接続詞［接続助詞］と共起する場合、第一の動詞から -hci は省略される。

entailment.quote: When co-occurring with a conjunction, the -hci is omitted from the first verb.

anchor.exact: The plural marker -ahci here agrees with the subject “the middle daughter and the youngest daughter”.

statement.en: In Karafuto Ainu, the plural marker -ahci/-hci on a transitive verb can agree with a plural subject even when the object is singular.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語において、他動詞の複数標識 -ahci/-hci は、目的語が単数であっても複数主語と一致しうる。

conditions: with plural subject and singular object

entailment.quote: The plural marker -ahci here agrees with the subject 'the middle daughter and the youngest daughter'.

anchor.exact: The subject is singular first person ku- ‘I’ and the object is the plural ku-mici-ihi-hcin ‘my grandsons’.

statement.en: In Karafuto Ainu, the verbal plural marker -hci can agree with a plural object when the subject is singular.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語において、主語が単数であっても、動詞の複数標識 -hci は複数目的語と一致しうる。

conditions: with singular subject and plural object

entailment.quote: The subject is singular first person ku- 'I' and the object is the plural ku-mici-ihi-hcin 'my grandsons'.

anchor.exact: When there are multiple possessors and the thing possessed is singular, -hcin is suffixed after the affiliative form suffix on the possessee.

statement.en: When there are multiple possessors and the possessee is singular in Karafuto Ainu, -hcin is suffixed after the affiliative suffix on the possessee to agree with the possessors.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語において、複数の所有者がいて被所有物が単数である場合、-hcin は被所有物の所属形接尾辞の後に付加されて所有者の一致を表す。

entailment.quote: When there are multiple possessors and the thing possessed is singular, -hcin is suffixed after the affiliative form suffix on the possessee.

anchor.exact: The plural marker -hcin in nanna-ha-hcin ‘older sister plural’ agrees with the two older sister possessees.

statement.en: When there is a single possessor and multiple possessees in Karafuto Ainu, the suffix -hcin attached after the affiliative suffix agrees with the plural possessees.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語において、単数の所有者に対して複数の被所有物がある場合、所属形接尾辞の後に付加された -hcin は複数被所有物の一致を表す。

entailment.quote: The plural marker -hcin in nanna-ha-hcin 'older sister plural' agrees with the two older sister possessees.

anchor.exact: Locative nouns can be followed by locative case particles like ta ‘locative case’, wa ‘ablative case’, and ene ‘allative case’ (ordinary nouns cannot be directly followed by a locative particle).

statement.en: Ordinary nouns cannot be directly followed by a locative case particle; only locative nouns can appear directly before them.
statement.ja: 普通名詞には直接格助詞が後続することはできず、位置名詞だけが格助詞の直前に現れることができる。

entailment.quote: Locative nouns can be followed by locative case particles like ta ... (ordinary nouns cannot be directly followed by a locative particle).

anchor.exact: Certain transitive verbs can only take locative nouns as objects. In such cases, an ordinary noun becomes the object in a pattern in which it is directly followed by a locative noun.

statement.en: Certain transitive verbs can only take locative nouns as their object.
statement.ja: ある種の他動詞は位置名詞のみを目的語に取ることができる。

entailment.quote: Certain transitive verbs can only take locative nouns as objects.

anchor.exact: If it is a location has already been mentioned or is already known, the antecedent to a locative noun can be omitted.

statement.en: The antecedent of a locative noun can be omitted if the location has already been mentioned or is already known.
statement.ja: すでに言及されたか既知である場所を表す場合、位置名詞の先行詞は省略できる。

entailment.quote: If it is a location has already been mentioned or is already known, the antecedent to a locative noun can be omitted.

anchor.exact: They can also directly follow a verb phrase without modification. In such a case, unlike the -hV neanpe pattern as in (11), the verb does not need a nominalizing suffix or a formal noun.

statement.en: Locative nouns can directly follow a verb phrase without modification, without requiring a nominalizing suffix or a formal noun.
statement.ja: 位置名詞は修飾なしに動詞句に直接後続することができ、その際、名詞化接尾辞や形式名詞を必要としない。

entailment.quote: They can also directly follow a verb phrase without modification. In such a case, unlike the -hV neanpe pattern as in (11), the verb does not need a nominalizing suffix or a formal noun.

anchor.exact: there are no examples of the bare root form san (< sam) in the Karafuto west coast northern dialects (Esutoru, Odasu).[117]

statement.en: In the northern dialects of the Karafuto west coast, there are no attested examples of the bare root form san (< sam) 'beside'.
statement.ja: 樺太西海岸北部方言（恵須取、小田洲）では、語根そのものの形である san (< sam) の用例は見られない。

entailment.quote: there are no examples of the bare root form san (< sam) in the Karafuto west coast northern dialects (Esutoru, Odasu).

anchor.exact: Furthermore, a number of locative nouns like kaa ‘above ~’ and soy ‘outside ~’ have no affiliative forms and always appear alone immediately followed by locative case particles.

statement.en: A number of locative nouns like kaa 'above' and soy 'outside' have no affiliative forms and always appear alone directly followed by locative case particles.
statement.ja: kaa「〜の上」や soy「〜の外」のようないくつかの位置名詞には所属形がなく、常に単独で直後に格助詞を伴って現れる。

entailment.quote: a number of locative nouns like kaa ‘above ~’ and soy ‘outside ~’ have no affiliative forms and always appear alone immediately followed by locative case particles.

anchor.exact: When a locative noun is followed by a simple locative case particle, it appears in its conceptual form and does not change to its affiliative form.

statement.en: When a locative noun is followed by a simple locative case particle, it appears in its conceptual form and does not change to its affiliative form.
statement.ja: 位置名詞に単純な格助詞が後続する場合、概念形で現れ、所属形には変化しない。

conditions: followed by simple locative case particle

entailment.quote: When a locative noun is followed by a simple locative case particle, it appears in its conceptual form and does not change to its affiliative form.

anchor.exact: The affiliative form of a locative noun is used with general, non-locative verbs to show the possessor or possessee of the verb’s subject or object.

statement.en: The affiliative form of a locative noun is used with non-locative verbs to show the possessor or possessee of the verb's subject or object.
statement.ja: 位置名詞の所属形は、一般的な非位置動詞とともに用いられ、その動詞の主語や目的語の所有関係（所有者または被所有者）を示す。

entailment.quote: The affiliative form of a locative noun is used with general, non-locative verbs to show the possessor or possessee of the verb’s subject or object.

anchor.exact: Place names and the words cise ‘house’ and kotan ‘village’ have the characteristics of both ordinary and locative nouns and can be followed either by the simple locative case particles ta, ne, or wa or by the compounded locative case particles.

statement.en: Place names and the words cise 'house' and kotan 'village' have characteristics of both ordinary and locative nouns, and can be followed by either simple locative case particles or compounded locative case particles.
statement.ja: 地名および cise「家」、kotan「村」という語は普通名詞と位置名詞の双方の性質を持ち、単純な格助詞あるいは複合格助詞のいずれをも後続させることができる。

entailment.quote: Place names and the words cise ‘house’ and kotan ‘village’ have the characteristics of both ordinary and locative nouns and can be followed either by the simple locative case particles ta, ne, or wa or by the compounded locative case partic

anchor.exact: In the Karafuto dialects, compounded locative case particles can follow either of the conceptual or the affiliative forms of ordinary nouns.

statement.en: In Karafuto dialects, compounded locative case particles can follow either the conceptual form or the affiliative form of ordinary nouns.
statement.ja: 樺太方言では、複合格助詞は普通名詞の概念形にも所属形にも後続することができる。

entailment.quote: In the Karafuto dialects, compounded locative case particles can follow either of the conceptual or the affiliative forms of ordinary nouns.

anchor.exact: For example, wahka ‘water’ almost is always in its conceptual form, always showing up as wahka onne or wahka ohta and never as ✶wahkaha ohta, ✶wahka ene or ✶wahka ta.

statement.en: The noun wahka 'water' almost always appears in its conceptual form followed by onne or ohta, and never as *wahkaha ohta, *wahka ene, or *wahka ta.
statement.ja: wahka「水」はほぼ常に概念形で現れ、wahka onne または wahka ohta として現れるが、*wahkaha ohta, *wahka ene, *wahka ta となることは決してない。

entailment.quote: wahka ‘water’ almost is always in its conceptual form, always showing up as wahka onne or wahka ohta and never as ✶wahkaha ohta, ✶wahka ene or ✶wahka ta.

anchor.exact: Furthermore, in showing the source of the noise, as in Hokkaido dialects, the allative case particle ene is used rather than the ablative case wa.

statement.en: In indicating the source of a noise, Karafuto Ainu, like Hokkaido dialects, uses the allative case particle ene rather than the ablative case wa.
statement.ja: 音の出所を示す際、北海道方言と同様に、樺太アイヌ語でも奪格 wa ではなく向格小辞 ene が用いられる。

conditions: showing the source of a noise

entailment.quote: in showing the source of the noise, as in Hokkaido dialects, the allative case particle ene is used rather than the ablative case wa.

anchor.exact: However, there are no examples of place names followed by ene from the dialects of the northern part of the Karafuto west coast.

statement.en: In the dialects of the northern part of the Karafuto west coast, there are no attested examples of place names followed directly by the allative case particle ene.
statement.ja: 樺太西海岸北部方言には、地名の直後に向格小辞 ene が後続する用例は見られない。

entailment.quote: there are no examples of place names followed by ene from the dialects of the northern part of the Karafuto west coast.

anchor.exact: Furthermore, there are no examples of the simple form wa of or-o-wa immediately following a noun affiliative form.

statement.en: In Karafuto Ainu, there are no examples of the simple ablative particle wa immediately following a noun affiliative form.
statement.ja: 名詞所属形の直後に or-o-wa の単純形 wa が直接後続する用例はない。

entailment.quote: there are no examples of the simple form wa of or-o-wa immediately following a noun affiliative form.

anchor.exact: In the latter case, unlike normal ordinary nouns, a locative case particle directly follows, and the affiliative form suffix is either pronounced extremely lightly or, in many cases, is dropped. Especially when the person form an- is attached, the result is almost without exception, an-cise ta.

statement.en: When cise 'house' is in its affiliative form and immediately followed by the locative particle ta, the affiliative suffix is pronounced lightly or dropped, surfacing almost without exception as an-cise ta with the person prefix an-.
statement.ja: cise「家」が所属形で格助詞 ta の直前に置かれる場合、所属形接尾辞は極めて弱く発音されるか脱落し、特に人称形式 an- がつく場合にはほぼ例外なく an-cise ta となる。

conditions: affiliative form of cise preceding ta

entailment.quote: the affiliative form suffix is either pronounced extremely lightly or, in many cases, is dropped. Especially when the person form an- is attached, the result is almost without exception, an-cise ta.

anchor.exact: The pronunciation of cise in cise ene is always just /cise/ and the suffix -he is never pronounced.

statement.en: In the phrase cise ene 'to the house', cise is always pronounced without the affiliative suffix -he.
statement.ja: cise ene における cise の発音は常に単に /cise/ であり、接尾辞 -he が発音されることは決してない。

entailment.quote: The pronunciation of cise in cise ene is always just /cise/ and the suffix -he is never pronounced.

anchor.exact: As with the singular affiliative form cise-he, the plural affiliative form cise-he-hcin can also be directly followed by the case particles ta and ene.[122] In such a case the affiliative suffix drops out giving cise-hcin. In addition, before the case particles ta and ene, the final -n of -hcin drops, leaving -hci.

statement.en: When the plural affiliative form cise-he-hcin is followed by ta or ene, the affiliative suffix -he drops out to give cise-hcin, and the final -n of -hcin also drops, leaving -hci.
statement.ja: 所属複数形 cise-he-hcin に格助詞 ta または ene が後続する場合、所属接尾辞が脱落して cise-hcin となり、さらに -hcin の末尾の -n も脱落して -hci となる。

entailment.quote: the plural affiliative form cise-he-hcin can also be directly followed by the case particles ta and ene. In such a case the affiliative suffix drops out giving cise-hcin. In addition, before the case particles ta and ene, the final -n of -h

anchor.exact: However, since an ordinary noun cannot be followed without any addition by a locative case particle, kotan is different from other ordinary nouns (and different, also, from cise ‘house’) and has probably become a locative noun or a place name in its conceptual form.

statement.en: In Karafuto Ainu, the noun kotan 'village' can take locative case particles directly in its conceptual form, unlike other ordinary nouns and unlike cise.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語において、kotan「村」は他の普通名詞や cise とも異なり、概念形のままで格助詞を直接伴うことができる。

entailment.quote: kotan is different from other ordinary nouns (and different, also, from cise 'house') and has probably become a locative noun or a place name in its conceptual form.

anchor.exact: Unlike Hokkaido dialects, in Karafuto Ainu a verb can be nominalized by the addition of -hV to the verb.

statement.en: In Karafuto Ainu, unlike Hokkaido dialects, a verb can be nominalized by suffixing -hV to the verb.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語では北海道方言と異なり、動詞に-hVを付加することで名詞化できる。

entailment.quote: Unlike Hokkaido dialects, in Karafuto Ainu a verb can be nominalized by the addition of -hV to the verb.

anchor.exact: If the verb ends in an open syllable, the suffix is formed using the final vowel, giving the forms -ha/-he/-hi/-ho/-hu.

statement.en: If a verb ends in an open syllable, the nominalizing suffix -hV is formed using the final vowel, yielding the forms -ha, -he, -hi, -ho, and -hu.
statement.ja: 動詞が開音節で終わる場合、名詞化接尾辞-hVは語末母音を用いて形成され、-ha, -he, -hi, -ho, -huという形をとる。

conditions: verb ends in an open syllable

entailment.quote: If the verb ends in an open syllable, the suffix is formed using the final vowel, giving the forms -ha/-he/-hi/-ho/-hu.

anchor.exact: If the verb ends in a closed syllable, -ihi is added.

statement.en: If a verb ends in a closed syllable, the nominalizing suffix -ihi is added.
statement.ja: 動詞が閉音節で終わる場合、名詞化接尾辞として-ihiが付加される。

conditions: verb ends in a closed syllable

entailment.quote: If the verb ends in a closed syllable, -ihi is added.

anchor.exact: A noun formed with this nominalizing suffix expresses an individual, specific event

statement.en: A noun formed with the -hV nominalizing suffix expresses an individual, specific event.
statement.ja: 名詞化接尾辞-hVによって形成された名詞は、個別的・具体的な出来事を表す。

entailment.quote: A noun formed with this nominalizing suffix expresses an individual, specific event

anchor.exact: while a noun formed not using the nominalizing suffix (treating an unmodified intransitive verb as a noun) expresses a general concept.

statement.en: A noun formed without the nominalizing suffix, by treating an unmodified intransitive verb as a noun, expresses a general concept.
statement.ja: 名詞化接尾辞を用いず、無変化の自動詞を名詞として扱うことで形成された名詞は、一般的な概念を表す。

entailment.quote: a noun formed not using the nominalizing suffix (treating an unmodified intransitive verb as a noun) expresses a general concept.

anchor.exact: Bugaeva (2016) points out that this nominalizing suffix is used in presuppositional contexts.

statement.en: The nominalizing suffix -hV is used in presuppositional contexts.
statement.ja: 名詞化接尾辞-hVは前提的な文脈で用いられる。

entailment.quote: Bugaeva (2016) points out that this nominalizing suffix is used in presuppositional contexts.

anchor.exact: As in Hokkaido dialects, an intransitive verb (or a 1-valence verb phrase) can be used as a noun expressing a general concept.

statement.en: As in Hokkaido dialects, an intransitive verb or a one-valence verb phrase can be used as a noun expressing a general concept in Karafuto Ainu.
statement.ja: 北海道方言と同様に、樺太アイヌ語でも自動詞（または1価の動詞句）は一般的な概念を表す名詞として用いることができる。

entailment.quote: As in Hokkaido dialects, an intransitive verb (or a 1-valence verb phrase) can be used as a noun expressing a general concept.

anchor.exact: In combination with the topical conjunctive particle neanpe, nominalization with the nominalizer -hV forms an expression that is used like a conjunction expressing a sequence of events ‘when ~ happened, the next event happened’.

statement.en: In combination with the topical conjunctive particle neanpe, nominalization with -hV forms an expression that is used like a conjunction expressing a sequence of events ('when ~ happened, the next event happened').
statement.ja: 主題接続助詞neanpeと組み合わさることで、名詞化辞-hVによる名詞化形は「〜した時、次の出来事が起きた」という出来事の連鎖を表す接続詞のように用いられる表現を形成する。

entailment.quote: In combination with the topical conjunctive particle neanpe, nominalization with the nominalizer -hV forms an expression that is used like a conjunction expressing a sequence of events ‘when ~ happened, the next event happened’.

anchor.exact: However, unlike the conjunction anah, the construction does not have a condition contrary to fact use.

statement.en: Unlike the conjunction anah, the -hV neanpe construction does not have a condition-contrary-to-fact use.
statement.ja: 接続詞anahとは異なり、-hV neanpe構文には反事実的条件の用法はない。

entailment.quote: However, unlike the conjunction anah, the construction does not have a condition contrary to fact use.

anchor.exact: A verb in its nominalized form with -ha/-he/-hi/-ho/-hu is sometimes used like a final particle.

statement.en: A verb in its nominalized form with -ha/-he/-hi/-ho/-hu is sometimes used like a sentence-final particle.
statement.ja: -ha/-he/-hi/-ho/-huによって名詞化された形の動詞は、終助詞のように用いられることがある。

entailment.quote: A verb in its nominalized form with -ha/-he/-hi/-ho/-hu is sometimes used like a final particle.

anchor.exact: Bugaeva (2016) points out that this presents old information and occurs in presuppositional contexts.

statement.en: The sentence-final particle use of nominalized verbs presents old information and occurs in presuppositional contexts.
statement.ja: 名詞化動詞の終助詞的用法は旧情報を提示し、前提的な文脈で生起する。

entailment.quote: Bugaeva (2016) points out that this presents old information and occurs in presuppositional contexts.

anchor.exact: Unlike the Hokkaido dialects, Karafuto Ainu has no first-person exclusive affixes ci- and -as.

statement.en: Unlike Hokkaido dialects, Karafuto Ainu lacks first-person exclusive affixes ci- and -as.
statement.ja: 北海道方言と異なり、樺太アイヌ語には1人称排他接辞 ci- および -as が存在しない。

entailment.quote: Unlike the Hokkaido dialects, Karafuto Ainu has no first-person exclusive affixes ci- and -as.

anchor.exact: The fourth person (indefinite person) affixes an-/-an do not have a separate first-person inclusive function, but are used as first-person singular forms, in addition to ku-.

statement.en: In Karafuto Ainu, the fourth-person (indefinite person) affixes an-/-an do not have a separate first-person inclusive function, but are used as first-person singular forms in addition to ku-.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語において、4人称（不定人称）接辞 an-/-an には独立した1人称包括の機能はなく、ku- に加えて1人称単数形として用いられる。

entailment.quote: The fourth person (indefinite person) affixes an-/-an do not have a separate first-person inclusive function, but are used as first-person singular forms, in addition to ku-.

anchor.exact: Hattori (1961) and Murasaki (1979) treat this as a stylistic difference with the “elders’ speech style” corresponding to the “elders’ language” in the lexicon.

statement.en: Hattori (1961) and Murasaki (1979) treat the first-person singular use of an-/-an as a stylistic difference corresponding to an elders' speech style.
statement.ja: 服部（1961）および村崎（1979）は、an-/-an の1人称単数としての用法を、語彙における「長老語」に対応する「長老層の文体」という文体差として扱っている。

entailment.quote: Hattori (1961) and Murasaki (1979) treat this as a stylistic difference with the “elders’ speech style” corresponding to the “elders’ language” in the lexicon.

anchor.exact: When speaking with an elder, young people use an-/-an as first-person affixes. This can be regarded as a kind of honorific language.

statement.en: When speaking with an elder, young speakers of Karafuto Ainu use an-/-an as first-person affixes, functioning as a kind of honorific language.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語では、若年層が長老と話す際に an-/-an を1人称接辞として用い、これは一種の敬語表現と見なすことができる。

entailment.quote: When speaking with an elder, young people use an-/-an as first-person affixes. This can be regarded as a kind of honorific language.

anchor.exact: Murasaki (1979) claims this usage is found in “elder → younger, elder → elder, and younger → elder” utterances.

statement.en: Murasaki (1979) claims that the first-person singular use of fourth person affixes is found in elder-to-younger, elder-to-elder, and younger-to-elder utterances.
statement.ja: 村崎（1979）は、4人称接辞の1人称単数での用法が「長老→若年者」「長老→長老」「若年者→長老」の発話に見られると主張している。

entailment.quote: Murasaki (1979) claims this usage is found in “elder → younger, elder → elder, and younger → elder” utterances.[123]

anchor.exact: unlike Hokkaido dialects, there is no distinction between inclusive “we” including the addressee (= ‘you and I’) and exclusive “we” excluding the addressee (= ‘(s)he and I’).[124] The forms an-/-an can be used for both.

statement.en: Unlike Hokkaido dialects, Karafuto Ainu lacks a clusivity distinction between inclusive and exclusive 'we', and the forms an-/-an can be used for both.
statement.ja: 北海道方言と異なり、樺太アイヌ語には聞き手を含む包括の「私たち」と聞き手を除外する排他の「私たち」の区別がなく、an-/-an が両方に用いられる。

entailment.quote: unlike Hokkaido dialects, there is no distinction between inclusive “we” including the addressee (= ‘you and I’) and exclusive “we” excluding the addressee (= ‘(s)he and I’). The forms an-/-an can be used for both.

anchor.exact: They are used for indefinite persons.

statement.en: In Karafuto Ainu, the fourth person affixes are used for indefinite persons.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語において、4人称接辞は不定人称を表すために用いられる。

entailment.quote: They are used for indefinite persons.

anchor.exact: They are used for the subject in an impersonal passive sentence. The agent is shown by the ablative case.

statement.en: In Karafuto Ainu, fourth person affixes are used for the subject in an impersonal passive sentence, with the agent expressed by the ablative case.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語では、4人称接辞は非人称受動文の主語に用いられ、動作主は奪格によって示される。

entailment.quote: They are used for the subject in an impersonal passive sentence. The agent is shown by the ablative case.

anchor.exact: They are used to show person in quoted sentences.

statement.en: In Karafuto Ainu, fourth person affixes are used to represent unspecified people speaking in quoted sentences.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語では、引用文中で発話者となる不特定の「人々」の人称を表すのに4人称接辞が用いられる。

entailment.quote: They are used to show person in quoted sentences.
entailment.note: Passage says only that they show person in quoted sentences, not that the speakers are unspecified people.

anchor.exact: in Karafuto dialects (Esutoru) an- appears when a first person and a second person plural are participating in a subject-object relation or an object-subject relation.

statement.en: In Karafuto Ainu (Esutoru), an- appears when a first person and a second person plural participate in a subject-object or object-subject relation.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語（恵須取方言）では、1人称と2人称複数が主語・目的語関係または目的語・主語関係にある際に an- が現れる。

entailment.quote: in Karafuto dialects (Esutoru) an- appears when a first person and a second person plural are participating in a subject-object relation or an object-subject relation.

anchor.exact: in Karafuto dialects the plurality of a second person objective case noun is shown by the presence or absence of -an.

statement.en: In Karafuto Ainu, when a first-person subject is combined with a second person, the plurality of a second-person object is marked by the presence or absence of -an.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語において、1人称主語が2人称と組み合わされる際、2人称目的語名詞の複数性は -an の有無によって標示される。

entailment.quote: when a first-person plural (an-) is combined with a second person, ... in Karafuto dialects the plurality of a second person objective case noun is shown by the presence or absence of -an.
